 Piastri denied qualifying chance as late-stage crash eliminates Aussie
 Sophie Wisely November 7, 2026 - 9.18pm 
 Powered by shares Share article Oscar Piastri endured his second consecutive Q2 exit after the Australian’s final flying lap in Brazil was agonisingly erased just as he crossed the finish line due to a rookie’s mistake. 
 Haas newbie Rafael Camara triggered by a late red flag on Sunday when he slammed heavily into the barriers and because the session was not restarted, Piastri was denied the chance to improve and finished the session in 12th place. 
 Qualifying was delayed for massive amounts of rain in Brazil.   Clive Mason 
 Advertisement Due to penalties, Piastri will start Monday’s race from 10th on the grid. 
 “I’d just finished a lap, but I think we probably went onto the inters a little bit too late and needed that extra lap or two to really get some temperature in them,” Piastri explained after qualifying. 
 “Some of the lines I was using on the wets definitely didn’t work on the inters, so some things to review, of course, but I think with another lap and maybe slightly better decisions we could have been there.
 “I definitely would have got one more lap in, but it’s the same for everybody,” Piastri continued about the red flag botching his lap. 
 “Everyone would have got another lap, so I’m not sure. I think there was definitely a lot more time out there, but you just need to be on the right tyre at the right time.
 “I think it’s going to be very challenging in the rain, so let’s see what we get.” 
 Read more
 Piastri leads tributes for the ‘Australian spirit’ of F1 compatriot 
 In contrast, Lando Norris secured McLaren’s third consecutive Brazilian Grand Prix pole position, mastering a chaotic qualifying session defined by torrential rain.
 Advertisement After a delay of over an hour to clear standing water at Interlagos, Norris navigated the treacherous conditions to top the Q3 shootout. 
 Clocking a 1:27.470s on intermediate tyres, he edged out Mercedes’ George Russell by two-tenths of a second.
 “It’s been a long day,” the pole sitter said after the lengthy qualifying. 
 “It’s not easy conditions out there, especially when you know it was going to rain a lot more.
 Advertisement Advertisement “It was about getting two laps in at the beginning, not making any mistakes, and that’s exactly what we did.”
 Despite his blistering pace, Russell will now forfeit the front row to serve a five-place grid penalty, promoting his teammate - newly-crowned world champion Kimi Antonelli - to second. 
 The demotion capped off a bitter session for Russell, who erupted over the team radio after being instructed to abort his final flying lap due to a miscommunication about incoming weather.
 Rain wrecked havoc on the session.   Clive Mason 
 Advertisement “Misjudgment on our side, we need to understand what happened. And yeah, the rain was coming and we should’ve just finished the lap,” he said. 
 A multitude of engine penalties will heavily shuffle the second row. 
 Ferrari’s Charles Leclerc set the fourth-fastest time but faces a 10-place grid drop, promoting Racing Bulls’ Liam Lawson to a career-best third and Audi’s Nico Hulkenberg to fourth.
 Max Verstappen, who already had a 30 place grid penalty for the engine chance from Red Bull, chose not to compete in Q2 due to the treacherous conditions and will start from the back of the grid. Joining him at the back of the grid is Lewis Hamilton and Sergio Perez.
